It is stated that on 24th November, 2015, as usual, the victim went to the school.
On that day, before leaving for school, she told her mother that she would be late in the evening as there was a birthday celebration of her friend in the school.

Therefore, on the next day i.e. 25 th November, 2015, the informant lodged a report at Bhadrawati Police Station and stated that he had a suspicion that the victim might have been kidnapped by the accused.

They went to the house of the accused to search him.

PW-7 has stated that their neighbour, Mary PW-6, accompanied them, and she took the victim to home.

In his evidence, he has stated that one lady by name Mary PW-6 took the victim to home.
He has stated that, on enquiry, the victim told that the accused had committed rape on her.
As far as the evidence of independent witness is concerned, it is also not consistent.
PW-2, the father of the victim, has not uttered a word about the date of the occurrence of the incident.
His evidence was recorded after the evidence of the victim.
He was expected to clear certain facts as to the date of the occurrence of the incident while giving evidence before the Court.
His evidence is conspicuously silent about the date of the incident.
As far as other witnesses are concerned, their -14- 207.CRI. APPEAL.196.2020.

Their evidence is contrary to the evidence of the victim.

In my view, therefore,
implicit reliance cannot be placed on such doubtful evidence.
14] The victim, on the date of the incident, was 13 years old.
The victim was a child, as understood by the provisions of the POCSO Act.
The testimony of such a witness needs to be carefully appreciated to rule out the possibility of tutoring.
There could be variety of reasons for false implication and ultimately tutoring the main witness in such cases.
The report lodged by the informant must be based on the true facts as to the crime.
The possibility of tutoring in such cases must be completely ruled out.

It is not out of place to mention that if there is material to suggest that the victim was tutored to make a statement before the police as well as at the time of her evidence in the Court, it can weigh against the case of the prosecution.
A statement made by the victim as a result of tutoring can lead to an inference of implication with an ulterior motive.
In this case, the victim, in her cross-examination, has given candid and categorical admissions that she was tutored by her father.
A girl child of 13 years of age is bound to feel pressure and make a statement desired by the parents.
In such cases, the possibility of tutoring, on proper appreciation of evidence, must be -15- 207.CRI. APPEAL.196.2020.
